description.narrative: StarTimes Smart Energy NIG Ltd (the Company or StarTimes Energy) is a subsidiary of StarTimes Group (StarTimes) which is leveraging its media business to expand into renewable energy in Nigeria. The proposed investment will support the Company to deploy up to 95 mini-grids (totalling 13.1MW) and 200,000 solar home systems (SHS) units. The mini-grid sites and SHS units are expected to receive performance-based grants from the World Bank Nigeria Distributed Access through Renewable Energy Scale-up Project (DARES). The debt investment is part of an up to US$200 million IFC DARES Platform under which IFC is looking to provide similarly structured debt investments to several mini grid developers/operators.

The project has benefitted from a climate and inclusion adjustment. The most significant expected project-level outcomes are improving the access, reliability, and affordability of electricity for consumers without access to power in Nigeria, with important environmental impact through GHG emissions savings. At the market level, IFC anticipates that the project will contribute to increase the competitiveness of the solar PV mini-grid market in Nigeria by using a programmatic approach to roll out mini-grid pipelines faster with demonstration potential in the region.
